questions.question: Five friends L, M, N, O, P, each has a different height. L is shorter than M but taller than N. O is shorter than N. P is taller than O. M is taller than P. Who among them is the tallest?
questions.solution:
**Given**: Five friends L, M, N, O, P, each has a different height.

L is shorter than M but taller than N.

→ M > L > N.

O is shorter than N. P is taller than O. M is taller than P. 

→ M > L > N > P > O.

Thus, M is the tallest.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 2".**

questions.question:
1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 are written on different faces of a dice. Three different positions of the same dice are shown below. Find the number on the face opposite to the one showing ‘2’. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/393961c677f3ad91fa16b1fc3fcc6e5bef64dda1c83431c8d481ef9248d1a419.png]
questions.solution:
To find the number on the face opposite to '2', we need to compare the given dice figures.

Comparing Figure 2 and Figure 3:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/00d88f7c7def6ee74a9a0f36db6d069c38fb711224c2549bf79f236c6f255d89.png] 

In Figure 2, the faces shown are 6, 3, 5.

In Figure 3, the faces shown are 2, 6, 3.

The common numbers in both figures are '6' and '3'.

When two positions of a single die are given, and two faces are common in both positions, then the remaining faces will be opposite to each other.

Therefore, from Figure 2 and Figure 3, the remaining faces are '5' and '2'.

→ '5' is opposite to '2'.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4".**

questions.question:
A & B means ‘A is the wife of B’.

A # B means ‘A is the father of B’.

A @ B means ‘A is the son of B’.

A % B means ‘A is the husband of B’.

A + B means ‘A is the mother of B’.

If A & B # C & D @ E % F + G, then how is C related to G?
questions.solution:
Family Chart:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a776c0a19b6706031165c847bcb98978a1e150482bd1260c12a74559ea55407.png] 

Decoding the Symbols:

 
 

 Symbol
 &
 #
 @
 %
 +
 
 

 Meaning
 Wife
 Father
 Son
 Husband
 Mother
 
 

 

Given: A & B # C & D @ E % F + G

Let's break down the relationships:

 
• A & B → A is the wife of B. (B is male)
 
• B # C → B is the father of C. (C's gender is unknown yet)
 
• C & D → C is the wife of D. (C is female, D is male)
 
• D @ E → D is the son of E. (E's gender is unknown yet)
 
• E % F → E is the husband of F. (E is male, F is female)
 
• F + G → F is the mother of G. (G's gender is unknown yet)

From the decoded relationships, we have:

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/adabde94d2ff1b89f3590ab1e8ff6b4a9cda4b52372c6103e9adadfc1603363f.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/48f3b4e5bdc0ec5f64e2619fb8674a8dccb356a7b595387b3f6f6e1c89d3fa23.png] 

Specifically, C is G's brother's wife, which means C is G's Sister-in-law.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

questions.question: Pointing to a man, Gaurav said, "He is the brother of the daughter of the father of my mother." How is that person related to Gaurav?
questions.solution:
Family Chart:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/854e449acd75259b0fdb6ee8f851931989fac9f98d9eedc211a9f6a75ae54a7d.png] 

Given: Pointing to a man, Gaurav said, "He is the brother of the daughter of the father of my mother."

Let's break down the statement from Gaurav's perspective:

 
• "my mother": This refers to Gaurav's mother.
 
• "father of my mother": This refers to Gaurav's maternal grandfather.
 
• "daughter of the father of my mother": This refers to the daughter of Gaurav's maternal grandfather. This could be Gaurav's mother or Gaurav's maternal aunt.
 
• "brother of the daughter of the father of my mother": This refers to the brother of either Gaurav's mother or Gaurav's maternal aunt.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/54b05a99c091b0370a030ba3e5babfcf1c25fa985a77928c7f3426ae7fb3f3b5.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2e9e756a2abc0310ca585456afc934c3b149bfe302a1120f8714d70e7d3730d7.png] 

 

In both cases, the person is Gaurav's Maternal Uncle.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the given sets.

(NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)

(18, 235, 29)

(7, 185, 30)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is: 

Logic: (first number + third number) × 5 = second number.

Let's test this logic with the given sets:

For **(18, 235, 29)**:

⇒ (18 + 29) × 5

= 47 × 5 = **235**. (This matches the second number)

For **(7, 185, 30)**:

⇒ (7 + 30) × 5

= 37 × 5 = **185**. (This matches the second number)

Now, let's apply this logic to the options:

1) **(32, 96, 16)**

⇒ (32 + 16) × 5 = 48 × 5 = 240.

This does not equal 96.

2) **(19, 576, 31)**

⇒ (19 + 31) × 5 = 50 × 5 = 250.

This does not equal 576.

3) **(23, 420, 10)**

⇒ (23 + 10) × 5 = 33 × 5 = 165.

This does not equal 420.

4) **(15, 210, 27)**

⇒ (15 + 27) × 5 = 42 × 5 = **210**.

**This matches the second number.**

Therefore, the set in which the numbers are related in the same way is **Option 4**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4".**
